source_record.Direction: increased midazolam exposure; reduced apparent oral clearance
source_record.Quantitative_Outcome: Table 1 (n=17; mean ± SD; berberine/control GMR and 90% CI): AUC0–∞ 45.08 ± 34.84 vs 65.18 ± 55.13 ng·h/mL; GMR 140% (117–168%), p<0.01. AUC0–12 h 39.79 ± 27.87 vs 57.71 ± 46.96 ng·h/mL; GMR 137% (112–167%), p<0.05. Cmax 15.30 ± 10.31 vs 20.88 ± 14.18 ng/mL; GMR 138% (107–177%), p<0.05. CL/F 70.25 ± 40.32 vs 53.35 ± 32.70 L/h; GMR 73% (60–89%), p<0.05. Midazolam/1′-hydroxymidazolam ratio at 1 h 6.91 ± 3.50 vs 10.34 ± 3.50; GMR 159% (130–194%), p<0.01. Table 1 Tmax 0.66 ± 0.33 vs 0.99 ± 0.37 h; GMR 152% (120–192%), p<0.05; t1/2 3.03 ± 1.11 vs 3.66 ± 1.53 h; GMR 119% (101–139%), p<0.05. The abstract prose swaps the Tmax and t1/2 labels; the Table 1 labels and values are retained, with the discrepancy disclosed.
source_record.Dose: Berberine capsules 300 mg orally three times daily (08:00, 16:00, 23:00) for 14 days; midazolam probe 2 mg administered before and at the end of each phase; 4-week washout.
source_record.Population: 18 healthy Chinese men entered; 17 completed (one withdrew because of a schedule conflict); age 21.6 ± 1.5 years and weight 61.35 ± 3.89 kg.
source_record.Study_Design: Two-phase randomized crossover; 14-day placebo and berberine phases separated by a 4-week washout; probe administered before and after each phase.

source_record.Interaction_Effect: Fisetin (20 μM) plus cabazitaxel (5 nM) reduced viability more than either agent alone in 22Rv1, PC-3M-luc-6 and C4-2 prostate cancer cells; the source-reported combination-index values indicate synergy for the measured combinations. Normal PrEC viability was minimally affected at these tested concentrations.
source_record.Mechanism: Cell experiments report reduced proliferation/colony formation and apoptosis-associated marker changes. These preclinical observations do not establish a clinical interaction mechanism.
source_record.Direction: Enhanced cell-viability inhibition under the tested in-vitro combination; combination-index classification is source/method specific.
source_record.Quantitative_Outcome: At 20 μM fisetin + 5 nM cabazitaxel, reported viability reductions were approximately 79% (22Rv1), 53% (PC-3M-luc-6) and 78% (C4-2), compared with fisetin-alone reductions of 45%, 49% and 74% and cabazitaxel-alone reductions of 32%, 11% and 38%, respectively. Table 1 reports CI 0.45676 for 22Rv1, 0.74663 for a row labelled “PC-3” (the Methods/Results identify PC-3M-luc-6; exact cell-line attribution is unresolved under V19-W13), and 0.72226 for C4-2. Methods define CI<0.9 as synergy, CI=1.1 as additive and CI>1.1 as antagonism; the Results also describe synergy as CI<1 (V19-W12). All three table values are below 0.9. CI values are reported from Table 1, not recalculated.
source_record.Dose: Fisetin 20 μM and cabazitaxel 5 nM for the reported cell-viability/CI combination; the Annexin V method describes 48 h fisetin followed by 24 h cabazitaxel. Do not assume that sequence applies to all assays.
source_record.Population: Human prostate cancer cell lines 22Rv1, PC-3M-luc-6 and C4-2; normal human prostate epithelial PrEC cells used as a comparison.
source_record.Study_Design: Controlled in-vitro cell-viability and colony-formation experiments with a fixed-dose combination and CompuSyn combination-index analysis. The source reports minimal effects on normal PrEC viability at the tested doses.

source_record.Interaction_Effect: In two prostate-cancer xenograft mouse models, fisetin plus cabazitaxel inhibited tumor growth more than either single agent under the reported regimens. The PC-3M-luc-6 model also assessed metastatic and angiogenesis-related endpoints.
source_record.Mechanism: Tumor marker findings include reduced proliferation/angiogenesis markers and apoptosis-associated changes; the article does not establish a human mechanism or clinical benefit.
source_record.Direction: Enhanced preclinical tumor-growth inhibition in the tested xenograft models.
source_record.Quantitative_Outcome: Two subcutaneous xenograft models used athymic nude male mice, four treatment groups and n=6/group; fisetin 20 mg/kg i.p. three times/week, cabazitaxel 5 mg/kg i.p. once/week, combination, or vehicle. In the 22Rv1 model, the article reports tumor-growth inhibition of 14% with fisetin, 36% with cabazitaxel and 53% with the combination versus control. In the PC-3M-luc-6 model, after the reported 7-week treatment course, tumor volume increased 9-fold with the combination, 22-fold with fisetin, 20-fold with cabazitaxel and 32-fold with control; combination versus control and single agents p=0.0001 in Results. Body-weight monitoring showed no apparent combination toxicity, but the data were not shown. Methods state treatment began 2 weeks after implantation; Results state 3 days for the PC-3M model (V19-W11).
source_record.Dose: Fisetin 20 mg/kg i.p. three times/week; cabazitaxel 5 mg/kg i.p. once/week; combination at the same doses; vehicle control. Source timing conflict for PC-3M model is retained under V19-W11.
source_record.Population: Two subcutaneous human prostate cancer xenografts in male athymic nude mice (6–8 weeks): 22Rv1 and metastatic PC-3M-luc-6; 24 mice per model, randomized into four groups of six.
source_record.Study_Design: Controlled in-vivo xenograft experiments with vehicle, fisetin, cabazitaxel and combination groups (n=6 each) and tumor-growth follow-up. Methods and Results conflict on treatment-start timing for the PC-3M-luc-6 model; see V19-W11.

source_record.Mechanism: The authors classify the clonazepam interaction as pharmacodynamic because serum and total-brain clonazepam concentrations did not significantly differ with PTE 100 mg/kg; this does not establish a human mechanism.
source_record.Direction: Pharmacodynamic potentiation reported in an acute mouse seizure-threshold model; no concentration change detected at the measured PTE dose.
source_record.Quantitative_Outcome: Clonazepam 0.04 mg/kg; pterostilbene (PTE) 25–100 mg/kg. Table 2(A), n=10/group at PTE 100: serum 16.40 ± 2.12 vs 14.28 ± 1.20 ng/mL (p=0.1977); total-brain 4.45 ± 0.61 vs 4.40 ± 0.32 ng/g tissue (p=0.4705). Figure 1 seizure-threshold means are not transcribed from the plots.
source_record.Dose: Clonazepam 0.04 mg/kg i.p.; PTE 25, 50 or 100 mg/kg i.p. 30 min before iv PTZ threshold testing. Separate Table 2 concentration comparison used PTE 100 mg/kg and n=10/group.

source_record.Interaction_Effect: No statistically significant caffeine pharmacokinetic or caffeine/paraxanthine-ratio difference was detected after repeated berberine under this study's analysis. The reported AUC/Cmax confidence intervals do not establish equivalence, so this is not evidence that the effect is exactly zero.
source_record.Mechanism: The outcomes are CYP1A2 (caffeine) or CYP2C19 (omeprazole) phenotyping-probe measurements; this small study found no statistically significant difference for these probes and does not establish the absence of an effect.
source_record.Direction: No statistically significant PK difference detected; caffeine AUC/Cmax estimates were lower with berberine, with confidence intervals crossing/breaching the 80% lower equivalence boundary.
source_record.Quantitative_Outcome: Table 1 (n=17; mean ± SD; berberine/control geometric mean ratio and 90% CI): caffeine 93 mg probe. AUC0–∞ 33.98 ± 9.40 vs 29.80 ± 11.30 μg·h/mL; ratio 85% (76–95%). Cmax 4.48 ± 1.03 vs 4.16 ± 1.86 μg/mL; 88% (75–103%). Tmax 0.96 ± 0.45 vs 1.00 ± 0.41 h; 108% (86–135%). t1/2 5.41 ± 1.81 vs 4.75 ± 1.15 h; 89% (78–102%). Plasma caffeine/paraxanthine ratio at 6 h: 1.51 ± 2.06 vs 0.94 ± 0.45; 80% (59–108%). Results state there were no statistically significant PK differences; Table 1 shows no significance marker. The article notes caffeine AUC0–∞ and Cmax did not meet its 80–125% bioequivalence criterion, despite nonsignificance, and cites small sample size as a possible explanation. This result is not evidence of equivalence or absence of effect.
source_record.Dose: Berberine capsules 300 mg orally three times daily for 14 days; caffeine 93 mg as a CYP1A2 probe before and at the end of each phase. The article describes 93 mg as the content of a standard cup of coffee; beverage composition is not otherwise characterized.
source_record.Population: 18 healthy Chinese male volunteers entered and 17 completed (one withdrew for a schedule conflict); age 21.6 ± 1.5 years and weight 61.35 ± 3.89 kg, mean ± SD.
source_record.Study_Design: Two-phase randomized crossover probe study with placebo and berberine periods, 4-week washout, and 14-day treatment per period. A five-drug cocktail was administered before and at the end of each period; plasma sampling continued through 12 h. Caffeine and its metabolite were measured as CYP1A2 indices.
source_record.Source_Title: Repeated administration of berberine inhibits cytochromes P450 in humans.
source_record.Authors: Guo Y, Chen Y, Tan ZR, Klaassen CD, Zhou HH.
source_record.Limitations: One small study in healthy young Chinese men (17 completers), one 14-day berberine-capsule regimen and one 93-mg caffeine probe. Nonsignificance does not prove no effect; reported caffeine AUC/Cmax 90% CIs do not lie wholly within 80–125% equivalence bounds. Berberine capsule salt/content/excipients and coffee beverage matrix are not fully characterized. Not an ordinary dietary interaction study or dose-equivalence assessment.
source_record.Confidence: Primary full-text randomized human probe study reviewed; small single-study evidence with source-reported estimates retained; independent expert re-review not performed.
source_record.Notes: V19-007: Table 1 values and source interpretation were transcribed; no inference of equivalence or a true null effect from nonsignificance.

source_record.Interaction_Effect: S-equol inhibited hOATP2B1-mediated estrone-3-sulfate uptake in vitro.
source_record.Mechanism: Competitive transporter uptake inhibition in the reported assay; not evidence of a clinical interaction.
source_record.Quantitative_Outcome: Ki=18.6 ± 5.6 μM; IC50 values across 0.5, 1, and 5 μM E3S were 13.0 ± 1.3, 28.2 ± 3.2, and 24.6 ± 2.4 μM.
source_record.Dose: S-equol concentration range 0–500 μM; E3S substrate 0.5, 1, or 5 μM.
source_record.Population: MDCKII cells transiently transfected with human OATP2B1/pCMV6; uptake measured at 37 °C for 2 min.
source_record.Study_Design: In-vitro transporter uptake concentration-response and kinetic inhibition study.

source_record.Authors: Navrátilová L, Applová L, Horký P, Mladěnka P, Pávek P, Trejtnar F
source_record.Limitations: Cell assay only. S-equol is produced only by equol-producing microbiomes from soy precursors; no intake-to-assay concentration bridge or human drug interaction was tested.

source_record.Interaction_Effect: Phloridzin inhibited OATP2B1-mediated estrone-3-sulfate uptake in a concentration-dependent in-vitro assay.
source_record.Mechanism: Kinetic analysis showed increased Km with no material Vmax change, consistent with competitive inhibition in this assay.
source_record.Quantitative_Outcome: IC50=110 μM for OATP2B1-mediated E3S uptake (Fig. 1); kinetic assay at 100 μM phloridzin increased Km while Vmax was not changed (Table 1).
source_record.Dose: Phloridzin concentration-response; kinetic comparison used 100 μM.
source_record.Population: HEK293 cells expressing human OATP2B1 and mock controls; [3H]E3S 5 nM, 37 °C, pH 7.4, 15 s for concentration-response assay.
source_record.Study_Design: Primary in-vitro transporter uptake concentration-response and kinetic assay; three independent experiments.

source_record.Authors: Takahashi Y, Narumi K, Nadai T, Ueda H, Yamamura T, Furugen A, Kobayashi M
source_record.Limitations: In-vitro result only. The same paper’s rat rosuvastatin experiments tested phloretin, not phloridzin; no clinical phloridzin interaction is established.
source_record.Confidence: Full-text compound-specific in-vitro primary evidence; dietary clinical relevance unknown.
source_record.Notes: No phloridzin Ki or clinical outcome claimed; IC50 and assay conditions transcribed from manuscript Fig. 1 caption and Results.

source_record.Preparation: Apple polyphenol test substance; supplier and lot specification not identified in reviewed passages.
